paragraphs.title: Building the Ark of the Covenant

easy.question: Who made the ark?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Bezaleel made the ark.”

easy.question: What material was the ark made from?
easy.explanation: The ark was made from shittim wood and then overlaid with gold.

easy.question: What was the ark overlaid with?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the ark was overlaid with pure gold both inside and outside.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the staves placed in the ark’s rings?
medium.explanation: The verse concludes that the staves were used “to bear the ark.”

medium.question: What does “the four corners” refer to in the description of the ark?
medium.explanation: The four rings were placed by the ark’s four corners, with two rings on each side.

medium.question: What was done before the staves were put into the ark’s rings?
answers: A gold crown was made for the ark
The ark was overlaid inside and outside
Four gold rings were cast for the ark
medium.explanation: First, four gold rings were cast; afterward, the staves were made and placed in the rings.

challenge.question: Which dimension of the ark was the greatest?
challenge.explanation: The ark was two and a half cubits long, while its breadth and height were each one and a half cubits.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the arrangement of the rings and staves?
answers: The rings were used to open the ark
The staves passed through the rings to allow stable carrying
The staves served as the ark’s cover
challenge.explanation: Two rings on each side allowed the staves to pass through them so the ark could be carried evenly.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “within and without” emphasize about the ark’s covering?
answers: Both the inside and outside were covered with gold
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that gold covered the ark on both its inner and outer surfaces.

questions.question: Which dimension of the ark was the greatest?
questions.explanation: The ark was two and a half cubits long, while its breadth and height were each one and a half cubits.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the arrangement of the rings and staves?
answers: The rings were used to open the ark
The staves passed through the rings to allow stable carrying
The staves served as the ark’s cover
questions.explanation: Two rings on each side allowed the staves to pass through them so the ark could be carried evenly.

questions.question: What does the phrase “within and without” emphasize about the ark’s covering?
answers: Both the inside and outside were covered with gold
questions.explanation: The phrase means that gold covered the ark on both its inner and outer surfaces.

paragraphs.title: The Mercy Seat and the Cherubim

easy.question: What was the mercy seat made from?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he made the mercy seat of pure gold.”

easy.question: How many cherubim were on the mercy seat?
easy.explanation: The passage describes two cherubim, one at each end.

easy.question: In which direction did the cherubim spread their wings?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the cherubim spread their wings “on high.”

medium.question: What were the dimensions of the mercy seat?
answers: Two and a half cubits by one and a half cubits
medium.explanation: The mercy seat was two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits broad.

medium.question: What does the phrase “beaten out of one piece” mean in this passage?
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the cherubim were fashioned as one piece with the mercy seat.

medium.question: Where was each cherub placed in relation to the mercy seat?
answers: Both were beneath the mercy seat
medium.explanation: The passage says, “One cherub on the end on this side, and another cherub on the other end.”

challenge.question: What can be understood from the description “with their faces one to another; even to the mercy seatward”?
answers: The cherubim faced one another and also toward the mercy seat
The cherubim faced away from one another
challenge.explanation: The verse says both that their faces were toward one another and that they faced toward the mercy seat.

challenge.question: What did the cherubim’s wings do in relation to the mercy seat?
challenge.explanation: The cherubim “covered with their wings over the mercy seat,” shielding it from above.

challenge.question: What is the order of the description in these verses?
answers: The cherubim, the mercy seat’s dimensions, then their wings
The cherubim’s wings, the mercy seat, then its dimensions
The making of the mercy seat, the making of the cherubim, then the description of their wings and faces
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 describes the mercy seat, verses 7–8 describe the cherubim, and verse 9 describes their wings and faces.

questions.question: What can be understood from the description “with their faces one to another; even to the mercy seatward”?
answers: The cherubim faced one another and also toward the mercy seat
The cherubim faced away from one another
questions.explanation: The verse says both that their faces were toward one another and that they faced toward the mercy seat.

questions.question: What did the cherubim’s wings do in relation to the mercy seat?
questions.explanation: The cherubim “covered with their wings over the mercy seat,” shielding it from above.

questions.question: What is the order of the description in these verses?
answers: The cherubim, the mercy seat’s dimensions, then their wings
The cherubim’s wings, the mercy seat, then its dimensions
The making of the mercy seat, the making of the cherubim, then the description of their wings and faces
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes the mercy seat, verses 7–8 describe the cherubim, and verse 9 describes their wings and faces.

paragraphs.title: Building the Table and Its Vessels

easy.question: What was the table made from originally?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he made the table of shittim wood.”

easy.question: What was the length of the table?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Two cubits was the length thereof.”

easy.question: Which vessels were made for the table?
easy.explanation: Verse 16 lists the vessels made for the table.

medium.question: What were the rings and staves on the table for?
answers: To attach a lamp to it
medium.explanation: The rings held the staves, which were used to carry the table.

medium.question: What was made after the table was overlaid with gold?
answers: Four rings were cast for it
A border was made around it
The vessels were placed on it
medium.explanation: After the gold covering and crown, the next verse describes making a border around the table.

medium.question: What does the phrase “a border of an handbreadth round about” describe?
answers: A boundary or frame around the table
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a handbreadth-high border extending around the table.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the rings and staves made for the table?
answers: The table was intended to be moved from place to place
The table was fastened to the floor
The table was meant to serve as a partition
challenge.explanation: The rings and staves made it possible to carry the table, showing that it was movable.

challenge.question: What was the relationship between the table’s dimensions?
answers: Its breadth was twice its length
Its length was twice its breadth
challenge.explanation: The table was two cubits long and one cubit broad, so its length was twice its breadth.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “his covers to cover withal”?
answers: They were intended to provide light
They were intended to cover the table
They were intended to pour with
challenge.explanation: The covers were vessels associated with covering or pouring, and the passage lists them among the table’s vessels.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the rings and staves made for the table?
answers: The table was intended to be moved from place to place
The table was fastened to the floor
The table was meant to serve as a partition
questions.explanation: The rings and staves made it possible to carry the table, showing that it was movable.

questions.question: What was the relationship between the table’s dimensions?
answers: Its breadth was twice its length
Its length was twice its breadth
questions.explanation: The table was two cubits long and one cubit broad, so its length was twice its breadth.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “his covers to cover withal”?
answers: They were intended to provide light
They were intended to cover the table
They were intended to pour with
questions.explanation: The covers were vessels associated with covering or pouring, and the passage lists them among the table’s vessels.

easy.question: What was the candlestick made from?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he made the candlestick of pure gold.”

easy.question: How many branches extended from the sides of the candlestick?
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says that six branches extended from it—three on each side.

easy.question: How many lamps were made for the candlestick?
easy.explanation: Verse 23 says, “And he made his seven lamps.”

medium.question: How many bowls were on the central shaft of the candlestick?
medium.explanation: Verse 20 says, “And in the candlestick were four bowls made like almonds.”

medium.question: What does “one beaten work” mean in this passage?
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the candlestick was fashioned as one unified piece.

medium.question: How were the six branches arranged?
answers: Two on one side and four on the other
medium.explanation: The passage says that three branches came from one side and three from the other.

challenge.question: How many bowls were there altogether on the six branches and the central shaft?
challenge.explanation: Each of the six branches had three bowls, making 18, and the central shaft had four more, for a total of 22.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof” teach?
answers: The candlestick was made from wood overlaid with gold
The candlestick and its vessels used one talent of gold
The candlestick used seven talents of gold
challenge.explanation: The verse says that one talent of pure gold was used to make the candlestick and all its vessels.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the statement that the bowls, knops, and flowers were “of the same”?
answers: They were brought from somewhere else
They were made from different materials
They were an integral part of the candlestick
challenge.explanation: The wording, together with “one beaten work,” emphasizes that these decorations formed part of the unified candlestick.

questions.question: How many bowls were there altogether on the six branches and the central shaft?
questions.explanation: Each of the six branches had three bowls, making 18, and the central shaft had four more, for a total of 22.

questions.question: What does the phrase “Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof” teach?
answers: The candlestick was made from wood overlaid with gold
The candlestick and its vessels used one talent of gold
The candlestick used seven talents of gold
questions.explanation: The verse says that one talent of pure gold was used to make the candlestick and all its vessels.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the statement that the bowls, knops, and flowers were “of the same”?
answers: They were brought from somewhere else
They were made from different materials
They were an integral part of the candlestick
questions.explanation: The wording, together with “one beaten work,” emphasizes that these decorations formed part of the unified candlestick.

easy.question: What was the incense altar made from?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he made the incense altar of shittim wood.”

easy.question: What were the dimensions of the incense altar?
answers: One cubit by two cubits, and one cubit high
One cubit by one cubit, and two cubits high
Two cubits by two cubits, and one cubit high
easy.explanation: It was one cubit long, one cubit broad, and two cubits high.

easy.question: What was the altar and its staves overlaid with?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the altar and its staves were overlaid with pure gold.

medium.question: What were the rings and staves for?
answers: To light a fire on it
medium.explanation: The rings held the staves, which were used to carry the altar.

medium.question: What does “foursquare” mean in the description of the altar?
answers: Square, with equal length and breadth
medium.explanation: The altar was one cubit long and one cubit broad, making it square.

medium.question: What was done after the rings were made for the altar?
answers: The rings were overlaid with silver
The staves were made and overlaid with gold
medium.explanation: The passage next says, “And he made the staves of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement that the horns were “of the same”?
answers: The horns were attached parts of the altar
The horns were made of fabric
The horns were separate carrying tools
challenge.explanation: The wording means that the horns came from the altar itself and were part of it.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the altar was decorated around its upper edge?
answers: The staves made from shittim wood
The crown of gold made around it
The two rings beneath the crown
challenge.explanation: The gold crown encircled the altar, showing that its upper edge was ornamented.

challenge.question: How many gold rings are explicitly mentioned for the altar?
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And he made two rings of gold for it.”

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that the horns were “of the same”?
answers: The horns were attached parts of the altar
The horns were made of fabric
The horns were separate carrying tools
questions.explanation: The wording means that the horns came from the altar itself and were part of it.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the altar was decorated around its upper edge?
answers: The staves made from shittim wood
The crown of gold made around it
The two rings beneath the crown
questions.explanation: The gold crown encircled the altar, showing that its upper edge was ornamented.

questions.question: How many gold rings are explicitly mentioned for the altar?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And he made two rings of gold for it.”

easy.question: What did Bezalel make according to the verse?
answers: The holy anointing oil and the pure incense
easy.explanation: The verse says that he made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices.

easy.question: How is the anointing oil described?
easy.explanation: The anointing oil is described as “holy.”

easy.question: How is the incense described?
easy.explanation: The verse describes the incense as pure incense of sweet spices.

medium.question: What does “according to the work of the apothecary” indicate about how these things were made?
answers: They were prepared skillfully and precisely
They were gathered from the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates professional and careful preparation, like the work of an apothecary.

medium.question: What did the anointing oil and incense have in common according to the verse?
answers: Both were intended to be eaten
Both were made according to the work of an apothecary
medium.explanation: The phrase “according to the work of the apothecary” applies to both items mentioned.

medium.question: What does the word “apothecary” refer to in this context?
answers: A person who prepares and mixes substances
A person who guards the tabernacle
A person who plays music in the sanctuary
medium.explanation: In the context of making oil and incense, an apothecary is someone skilled in preparing and mixing substances.

challenge.question: What conclusion fits the fact that the oil is called “holy” and the incense “pure”?
answers: They had special status and qualities for sacred worship
They were used only for ordinary purposes
They were ordinary materials without significance
challenge.explanation: The words “holy” and “pure” emphasize their importance and suitability for sacred worship.

challenge.question: Why does the verse likely emphasize “according to the work of the apothecary” after mentioning both substances?
answers: To emphasize that their preparation required skilled work
To explain where the substances were stored
challenge.explanation: The phrase gives information about the quality and method of preparation, not about a priest or storage place.

challenge.question: What does the verse indicate about the function of the incense when it calls it “pure incense of sweet spices”?
answers: It was a mixture intended to be burned and produce a fragrance
It was a vessel made of gold
challenge.explanation: Incense is a fragrant mixture burned to release a pleasant aroma.

questions.question: What conclusion fits the fact that the oil is called “holy” and the incense “pure”?
answers: They had special status and qualities for sacred worship
They were used only for ordinary purposes
They were ordinary materials without significance
questions.explanation: The words “holy” and “pure” emphasize their importance and suitability for sacred worship.

questions.question: Why does the verse likely emphasize “according to the work of the apothecary” after mentioning both substances?
answers: To emphasize that their preparation required skilled work
To explain where the substances were stored
questions.explanation: The phrase gives information about the quality and method of preparation, not about a priest or storage place.

questions.question: What does the verse indicate about the function of the incense when it calls it “pure incense of sweet spices”?
answers: It was a mixture intended to be burned and produce a fragrance
It was a vessel made of gold
questions.explanation: Incense is a fragrant mixture burned to release a pleasant aroma.
